title.narrative: Accelerating the transition to a net-zero, nature-positive economy in Costa Rica

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project will lead to important co-benefits. While the central objective of the project is to support Costa Rica in the implementation of its National Decarbonization Plan, the project will contribute to improve coordination, build capacity and strengthen knowledge management of government institutions as well as private stakeholders. Expected co-benefits include:Social:· Increased institutional capacity: enhancing the ability of organizations and institutions to effectively respond to and mitigate the impact of natural disasters including extreme weather events through improved planning, resource allocation. This will increase community resilience and reduce the social and economic impact of such events.· Comprehensive modelling enhances resilience of value chains by assessing the interconnectedness between climate change, biodiversity loss and economic activities. By integrating climate-nature interactions into modelling efforts, decision-makers can also gain insights into the return on different investments by sector and the environmental footprint of different industries and supply chains. This approach helps identify opportunities to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, minimize habitat destruction, and enhance resource efficiency throughout the production process while promoting growth in jobs and income. Moreover, comprehensive modelling allows decision makers to examine trade-offs and make informed decisions in developing of strategies to promote sustainable practices, enhance resilience to environmental risks, and foster the transition towards nature-positive and climate-resilient economies. · Inclusion of vulnerable groups, gender and youth considerations into climate and nature initiatives: the transition to a net-zero nature-positive future has winners and losers. Through the support of the Global Platform, the project will promote the integration of diverse perspectives and needs into socio-economic modelling and NZNP planning, to ensure that countries can successfully plan for and navigate to a NZNP which is climate just.Economic:· Improved returns on public investment through rigorous analysis of investment scenarios across key sectors of the economy: by examining different investment options, policy makers will be positioned to increase the economic efficiency and gains of allocation decisions in key sectors and increase job, growth and sustainability multipliers of both public and private capital flows. · Job creation and economic growth: the transition to a net-zero and nature-positive economy is expected to create new job opportunities (especially green jobs), stimulate innovation, research and development that also promote economic growth, particularly in key identified sectors for downstream intervention such as sustainable agriculture and industry.Project Cost Effectiveness The project will support Costa Rica in the implementation of its National Decarbonization Plan, leading to environmental, social and economic benefits. Through achievement of its intended outcomes, the project is expected to be transformative in supporting Costa Rica in achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, therefore contributing to the Global Environmental Benefits. The project is expected to achieve greenhouse gas emissions mitigation of 1,440,293 tonnes of CO2eq (GEF core indicator 6), restoring 3,000 ha of land (GEF core indicator 3) and improving practices in 75,000 ha (GEF core indicator 4). In addition, the number of direct beneficiaries, through training, capacity building activities, piloting and scaling up in value chains, is expected to reach 3300 of which 50% are expected to be women. In addition, expected co-benefits include increase institutional capacity, enhance resilience, inclusion of vulnerable groups, improve returns on public investment and job creation.These results are expected to be achieved through a cost-effective project design, that builds on the expertise of the implementing partners (UNEP, FAO), the executing agency (Fundecooperación) and key stakeholders. The project execution will rely on a efficient core team structure and specific consultancies selected through procurement process that will ensure it cost-effectiveness. The cost of the project, resources, and efforts would then be marginal compare to all the benefits across multiple sectors with multiple actors participating and advancing toward sustainable development and the ultimate goals and objectives of the Paris Agreement.
To strengthen Costa Rican institutions to accelerate nature-positive, net-zero pathways.
